title: Baška Voda with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Costs
metaDescription: Planning a trip to Baška Voda with a dog: the dog beach at Stazica, rules for restaurants and ferries, accommodation fees, heat, vets and EU pet passport.
content:
## Dog Beach in Baška Voda: Where Dogs Can Swim

Baška Voda has one dog-friendly stretch, on **Stazica beach**, a pebble beach about 500 m long. The dog section runs between two sets of steps down to the beach. One is roughly 200 m south of the Milenij aparthotel. The other is northwest of the **Oseka** beach bar. Signs for pet owners are placed at the top and bottom of those stairs and at the Milenij aparthotel. The spot is a short walk, around 3 minutes, from the centre. It has a car park next to it, small pebbles and natural shade from trees.

There is no official, fenced "plaža za pse" with dog showers or dedicated lifeguards of the Krk or Crikvenica kind. It is a marked section of an ordinary beach. Searching "plaža za pse" on a map app brings it up.

### Are Dogs Allowed on Other Beaches in Baška Voda?

No. Other approaches to Stazica and the other town beaches carry signs prohibiting dogs. Fines for ignoring them are possible, and beach staff do check in July and August. Keep the dog within the marked section and carry waste bags.

### Beaches Nearby

The Makarska Riviera has very few official dog beaches, so Baška Voda is better placed than most neighbours. Brela, a few kilometres to the northwest, has a dog-friendly beach called Stomarica. Rules change from season to season, so check the signs on arrival.

## Old Town, Promenade and Restaurants

The old town is small and compact, with narrow lanes and a seafront promenade. Dogs on a leash are normal here. The promenade has little shade, and stone paving gets very hot at midday, so walk before 9:00 or after 19:00.

Restaurants usually allow dogs on outdoor terraces. Indoor rooms are generally off-limits because of hygiene rules for food service. Ask before sitting down, and bring a collapsible water bowl, since many places will provide water but not always a bowl. Dogs are not allowed in shops selling food, markets or bakeries.

## National Parks and Nature Parks

Baška Voda sits below the **Biokovo Nature Park**, where dogs on a leash are generally accepted on trails. Summer ground temperatures on the exposed limestone are punishing, and there is almost no surface water on the mountain. Carry at least 1 litre of water per dog for any hike.

Further afield, rules are stricter. Plitvice Lakes does not accept dogs. Krka and some other parks limit pets to certain zones, so confirm on the park's official page before a day trip.

## Ferries and Catamarans With a Dog

Brač and Hvar are the usual day trips from this coast. Jadrolinija carries pets free of charge on its ferry and passenger-ship lines. Dogs must be on a leash and wear a muzzle, except assistance dogs.

The rules differ by vessel:

- **Car ferries:** large dogs (over 8 kg) travel on the open deck.
- **Catamarans:** small pets in a carrier up to 45 x 35 x 25 cm and a total weight of 8 kg can stay in the lounge. Larger dogs cannot go inside.
- Operators have changed policies mid-season, so check the day before departure.

The Makarska–Sumartin (Brač) ferry is the simplest option for a dog. The car deck is open and the crossing is short, about 1 hour.

## What Accommodation Charges for a Dog

Private apartments and rooms in the Makarska Riviera typically charge **€5–15 per night** for a dog, or a flat cleaning fee. Hotels usually charge **€10–25 per night**, and some limit dogs to certain rooms or cap the weight. Some hosts accept dogs free off-season. Pet-friendly listings are far fewer than the total number of rooms, so filter for it and confirm in writing before paying a deposit.

**Insider tip:** Baška Voda is steep above the seafront. Choose a place on the flat strip between the promenade and the main road if the dog is old or large. Climbing at 30 °C is hard on both of you.

## Summer Heat: Best Months to Visit

July and August bring air temperatures of 30–35 °C, hot pavement and crowded beaches. Dogs overheat quickly, and the pebbles at the shore burn paws. Avoid walks between 11:00 and 17:00 and never leave a dog in a parked car.

- **May–June:** the best choice. Warm sea, mild days, empty paths.
- **September–October:** sea still warm, fewer people, more flexible hosts.
- **July–August:** manageable only with early and late walks and a shaded base.

Sea urchins are common on rocky edges, so water shoes for dogs help if the dog swims off the pebbles. Ticks are present on Biokovo trails and in scrub; check the dog after every walk.

## Vets and Health Basics

Makarska, about 15 km away, has several veterinary clinics, and Split has 24-hour emergency vets, roughly 55 km northwest. Baška Voda itself has no major clinic, so save a vet's number before arrival. Ask your hosts for the nearest one. Pharmacies do not sell veterinary prescription medicines.

Ticks, fleas and sandflies are the main concerns. Ask your own vet about tick prevention and leishmaniasis protection for Mediterranean regions before leaving. Fresh water is available on the promenade, but carry your own for walks. Croatia requires all dogs to be microchipped, and a leash is required in public places.

## EU Pet Passport and Entry Rules

Dogs travelling to Croatia from another EU country need three things:

1. An **ISO microchip**, implanted before the rabies vaccine.
2. A **rabies vaccination** given at least 21 days before travel and kept up to date.
3. An **EU pet passport** (or the equivalent document under the current rules).

A new EU framework applied from 22 April 2026, but the requirements for ordinary travellers remain essentially the same and existing passports stay valid. A maximum of five pets per owner can travel under non-commercial rules. Travellers from outside the EU (UK, USA) use an animal health certificate instead of a passport. A tapeworm treatment is not required for entry to Croatia. Croatia has no quarantine for dogs entering with correct documents. Some breeds may face restrictions on home-country return; check the rules of the country you are travelling back to.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Baška Voda?

**Baška Voda is moderately dog-friendly: 3.5 out of 5.** The Stazica dog section is good, with small pebbles, shade and a bar next door, and it is the only legal swim spot for a dog in town. That is a real advantage on a coast where most resorts offer nothing. The Krk beach of Vela Plaža is better equipped, but it is hundreds of kilometres away. Baška Voda does not suit a dog that wants to roam every beach. The "dog-friendly" label is generous: one section, banned everywhere else, steep streets and little shade in July. Visit in May, June or September, stay near the Stazica end, and the trip works well.

faq.question: Does Baška Voda have an official dog beach?
faq.answer: Yes, a signed dog section of Stazica beach near the Oseka beach bar. It lies between two staircases, one about 200 m south of the Milenij aparthotel. Other town beaches have signs banning dogs.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in restaurants in Baška Voda?
faq.answer: Usually on outdoor terraces, on a leash, but not inside. Ask the staff first and bring your own bowl.

faq.question: Do dogs travel free on ferries from Makarska?
faq.answer: On Jadrolinija ferry lines, pets travel free. Dogs must be leashed and muzzled; those over 8 kg stay on the open deck. On catamarans, only small pets in a carrier up to 8 kg are allowed inside.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia from the EU?
faq.answer: An ISO microchip, a rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, and an EU pet passport. No quarantine or tapeworm treatment is required.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Baška Voda with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June, September and October. Summer highs of 30–35 °C in July and August make midday walks unsafe, and hot pebbles can burn paws.

faq.question: How much does accommodation charge for a dog?
faq.answer: Apartments and rooms typically charge €5–15 per night. Hotels charge about €10–25 per night. Always confirm the fee and any weight limit before booking.

quickAnswer: Baška Voda is moderately dog-friendly. It has one signed dog section on Stazica beach near the Oseka beach bar, about 3 minutes from the centre. Dogs are banned on its other beaches. Restaurants and the old town are easy with a leash. Visit in May, June or September–October. An EU pet passport, microchip and rabies vaccination are required.
